answer: In an agent economy, reputation is earned only by fresh verifiable work and decays daily like a fading echo: each contribution sends a ripple of signed, timestamped receipts across peers, while idle days shrink the score toward zero. A cloned dormant identity gains nothing because its copy starts at zero and only grows if the operator supplies new signed work. So flooding the network with sybils costs real compute plus accepted labor per clone, more than any attack gain, like shouting into a canyon that answers only effort.
